topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and mechanisms of drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit inherent biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, such as hormone dependency, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, mechanisms, and clinical challenges of targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and managing subsequent drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic mechanisms of targeting cancer-specific cell surface antigens using unconjugated monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-mediated interventions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and clinical strategies to harness immune responses against cancer, including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Global challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overall historical progress, ongoing therapeutic dilemmas, role of prevention and biomarkers, and future paradigms in managing cancer.
